meta.title: MCO · One review, individual provider answers
meta.subtitle: Default review path · CLI or MCP → shared Python runtime → local provider CLIs · pinned source 3cfce13

components.label: Review entry points
components.explanation: One request supplies repo, prompt, selected providers and target paths. CLI calls the workflow directly; FastMCP serves stdio and offloads _sync_review with asyncio.to_thread. CLI --json prints the payload without per-output stderr and exits with its exit_code. MCP returns {ok:true,data:payload}; that envelope means execution returned, not that every provider succeeded. Invalid MCP input returns {ok:false,error:{code,message}}.

components.label: Validate & plan
components.explanation: Reject unknown providers or invalid scope before execution. MCP rejects unsupported execution modes and derives provider permission flags; CLI checks provider policy and strict-enforcement failures. default_invocations makes one invocation per selected provider, with its configured model and scope. Scope paths must stay within the repo and allow_paths. Read-only is a provider-specific mode, not an independently established universal OS isolation guarantee.

components.label: Concurrent invocation runtime
components.explanation: run_invocation_workflow delegates to run_invocations when chain, debate and synthesis are off. A thread-pool job runs _run_one_invocation for each selection. max_provider_parallelism > 0 caps workers; 0 allows all invocations concurrently. Each job creates TaskInput, calls adapter.run, polls status, reads stdout logs, decodes output, and optionally emits deltas. Stall, per-invocation hard and global deadlines constrain execution; timeout or cancellation calls adapter.cancel. Worker exceptions become that invocation's failed result, not a fabricated answer.

components.label: Provider adapters · shim
components.explanation: adapter_registry() defaults to provider-specific shim adapters. ShimAdapterBase builds the command, opens raw stdout/stderr logs, spawns the process with cwd=repo_root, and returns a TaskRunRef. poll checks process completion; cancel terminates the process. Provider decoders normalize transport output: Codex parses JSON events, while providers without a decoder use raw stdout. This box represents one adapter per selected provider, not a remote MCO service.

components.label: Collect individual results
components.explanation: This is the collection responsibility inside run_invocations, not another service. Each result retains invocation_id, provider, model, status, output, error, exit_code, deltas, transport_status and stderr. Futures finish independently but are stored by original index. All successes → complete; some → partial; none → failed. Return payload includes task_id, stage, outputs, aggregate status, exit_code and artifact_root. No default synthesis or consensus step replaces the individual answers.

components.label: Local run artifacts
components.explanation: Runtime allocates provider-runs and answer files. Adapters capture raw process logs; runtime streams decoded answers into per-invocation Markdown. CLI artifact/both modes (or --save-artifacts) retain the run and write run metadata; otherwise a TemporaryDirectory is cleaned and returned artifact paths are null. MCP _sync_review does not enable persist_artifacts, so its default files are temporary. This is a filesystem boundary, not a database server.

components.label: Selected provider processes
components.explanation: Only the selected provider commands execute, with the repository as working directory and the prompt in their arguments. Claude requests text output; Codex requests JSON events. These executables are outside the MCO Python process. Provider-side model execution, network calls and authentication internals are not established by this checkout and are intentionally not drawn.

boundaries.label: MCO Python process · logical responsibilities, not separate services

cards.title: One request → separate answers
items: Same prompt and scope fan out by default; configured models stay attached.
Each output preserves its provider identity and failure; no implicit merger.

cards.title: Execution & failure semantics
items: Parallelism is bounded when configured; deadlines cancel stalled work.
Read-only maps to provider flags; actual provider isolation is not proven here.

cards.title: Scope of this diagram
items: Default shim, no chain/debate/synthesis; CLI ACP and custom transports omitted.
Provider backends and network/auth internals are outside the checked-out code.
